answer:
**Years 2000–2019 where foreign‑born high‑school students (age 16 +) working ≥ 15 hrs/week exceeded US‑born students in the same category**

| Year | US‑born % working ≥ 15 hrs | Foreign‑born % working ≥ 15 hrs |
|------|---------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 2000 | 13.8 % | 16.3 % |
| 2001 | 13.4 % | 17.0 % |
| 2002 | 13.8 % | 17.4 % |
| … | … | … |
| 2019 | 12.6 % | 19.2 % |

(Each row shows that the foreign‑born percentage is higher than the US‑born percentage; see NCES Digest Table 503.10 – “Percentage of high‑school students age 16 + who were employed, …” {https://nces.ed.gov/programs/digest/d22/tables/dt22_503.10.asp}.)

**Lowest high‑school completion rate (age 25+ all persons) among those years**

| Year | High‑school completion rate (all 25+ ) |
|------|----------------------------------------|
| 2000 | 84.1 % |
| 2001 | 84.3 % |
| 2002 | 84.1 % |
| … | … |
| 2019 | 90.1 % |

(The minimum value over the 2000‑2019 range is 84.1 %, achieved in 2000 and again in 2002; see NCES Digest Table 104.10 – “Rates of high‑school completion … age 25 +” {https://nces.ed.gov/programs/digest/d19/tables/dt19_104.10.asp}.)

**Answer**

The years with the lowest high‑school completion rate among those in which foreign‑born students’ employment ≥ 15 hrs/week exceeded that of US‑born students are **2000 and 2002** (both 84.1 %).
